A Community Well-Being score from the census profile

Source: R/census.R
cnscwb.Rd

Indigenous Services Canada's Community Well-Being (CWB) index (cwbscr) computed from the public 2021 Census Indigenous Population Profile, for each geography and group.

Usage

cnscwb(
  x,
  dwell = NULL,
  groups = c("First Nations", "Métis", "Inuit", "Non-Indigenous"),
  bounds = c(2650, 75000),
  resid = "Total - Residence on or off reserve",
  minpop = 250
)

Arguments

x

A cnsprof of a population table.

dwell

Optional cnsprof of the matching household table.

groups

The groups to score (default First Nations, Metis, Inuit and non-Indigenous people).

bounds

Income bounds of cwbscr.

resid

On or off reserve, in the tables that split it (default the total).

minpop

The smallest population scored (default 250; the Department uses 65).

Value

A data frame of class rmbl_census_cwb: geo, dguid, group; the components income, education, housing, labour and the score cwb (0 to 100, NA where not scored); and the inputs incpercap (dollars), highsch25p, uni25p, population, participation, employment, nomajrep, notcro (percentages).

Details

The Department computes the CWB from census microdata; the public profile gives close but not the same inputs, and this function says where it departs:

income

per capita: the number of total income recipients aged 15 and over times their average total income, over the population in private households (all ages), as the CWB does.

education

the shares with at least a high school diploma (all but those with no certificate, diploma or degree) and with a bachelor's degree or higher, both among those aged 25 and over: the profile has no age group of 20 and over, which the CWB uses for the first.

labour force

the participation rate and the employment rate of participants (100 less the unemployment rate) of those aged 25 to 64: the CWB uses 20 to 64.

housing

the shares of households with one person or fewer per room and needing no major repairs, from the household profile (dwell), which splits Indigenous from non-Indigenous households only, so First Nations, Metis and Inuit people all get the pooled Indigenous households' housing: the CWB counts persons, not households. Without dwell the housing component and the score are NA.

A group of fewer than minpop people in a geography gets no score. The Department scores communities of 65 people or more; the default here is 250, because the public profile's counts are rounded to multiples of 5 and its long-form counts rest on a few dozen households at that size. Geographies are matched by DGUID, so places that share a name stay apart. The inputs are those of the 2021 profile (98-510-X2021001 to -016): other editions name their characteristics differently. Read the result as a CWB-style description of socio-economic conditions, close to but not the Department's index, and never as a measure of the wellness of First Nations, Metis or Inuit people as they define it (see cwbscr).

References

Indigenous Services Canada (2019). Report on trends in First Nations communities, 1981 to 2016 (Community Well-Being index).
sac-isc.gc.ca/eng/1345816651029/1557323327644

See also

cwbscr.

Examples

p <- cnsprof(indiex("censuspop"))
h <- cnsprof(indiex("censushh"))
cnscwb(p, h)[, c("geo", "group", "income", "education", "housing", "labour",
                     "cwb")]
